What the numbers say

For the session of Tuesday, November 24, 2026, the DappGo regime model reads the tracked universe (36 US-listed stocks and ETFs on DappGo's reviewed watchlist) as risk-off. SPY is below its 50-day average and below its 200-day average; its 20-day trend is down and realised volatility is in the high band.

4 of 36 tickers (11%) are priced above their own 20-day moving average, and 11 of 34 (32%) above their 200-day average. Below 30% is the level the model treats as weak breadth, which is enough on its own for a risk-off reading. On the day 9 rose and 27 fell; the median move was −1.31%.

Among sectors with at least two tracked names, Healthcare had the strongest average move at +3.05% and Technology the weakest at −5.77%, a spread of 8.82 percentage points. The standard deviation of sector averages was 3.54 points; a larger figure means sectors moved less in step.

1 ticker has a 14-day RSI at or below 30 (SNDK), and none is at or above 70. An RSI extreme records how one-sided recent trading has been. It is not, by itself, evidence that the move is about to reverse.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-11-23), the share of tickers above the 20-day average held at 11%, and the regime reading stayed risk-off.
